chase_cards.name: Unown R [CoroCoro Comic November 2000]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is a quiet letter with a loud boundary. R sits beside J as a Generation II Unown form outside the normal Neo expansion run, but unlike J it did not get an English Wizards-era counterpart.

key_artists.name: Hideki Kazama
key_artists.why: Kazama matters here because the card is almost pure sign-language: a letter, a Pokémon, and a promo object. The art credit helps preserve the graphic alphabet lane without letting artist identity replace route evidence.

claims.text: The local catalog models the CoroCoro Comic November 2000 issue insert source group as one row containing Unown R at source index 209.
Bulbapedia places the Japanese Unown R print in Unnumbered Promotional cards and identifies its release as a CoroCoro Comic November 2000 issue insert on October 15, 2000.
Bulbapedia identifies Unown R as a Psychic-type Basic Pokémon card with 30 HP, the Reassure Pokémon Power, and the Hidden Power attack.

Bulbapedia says the Generation II Unown forms J and R were not released in a Japanese or English expansion; they were instead released as Japanese Unnumbered Promotional cards and, for J only, as an English Wizards Black Star Promo.
Bulbapedia credits the Unown R artwork to Hideki Kazama.
Bulbapedia's Hideki Kazama category includes multiple Unown letter cards, tying Kazama's early TCG credit surface to the alphabet-creature lane.
Bulbapedia says Unown R would not be released outside Japan until the EX Unseen Forces expansion.

As judged collector texture, Unown R matters because it is the other half of the J/R Neo-era gap, but its route is sharper: CoroCoro in Japan, no English Wizards-era counterpart, and a later localization boundary.

narrative.human_title: CoroCoro November 2000 Unown R: the letter with no easy English twin
narrative.why_it_matters: Unown R is quiet, but it teaches the catalog something important. J and R are the Neo-era letters that escaped the normal expansion grid, yet R takes the stranger path: a CoroCoro insert in Japan, no Wizards Black Star echo, and no non-Japanese release until much later. It is exactly the kind of card an agent can misread if it treats Unown as a flat alphabet instead of an assembly of magazines, languages, and release decisions.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, seller story, slab label, or agent memory says Unown R, アンノーンR, CoroCoro Comic November 2000, October 15 2000, Wizards Promo, Spell of the Unown, EX Unseen Forces, Neo Unown, Hideki Kazama, or Unown alphabet set.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify Unown R by CoroCoro Comic November 2000 insert route, source index 209, Japanese unnumbered promo status, and no-Wizards-counterpart boundary before trusting name-only Unown matching.
steps: Confirm the card is Unown R, not another Unown letter.
Preserve the source route: CoroCoro Comic November 2000 issue insert, October 15, 2000, local source index 209.

Check that the object is being treated as a Japanese Unnumbered Promotional card, not as English Wizards Black Star Promo 38, a nonexistent Wizards Unown R counterpart, EX Unseen Forces, or a Neo expansion row.
Use the Reassure / Hidden Power card text as contextual support, not as a substitute for row identity.
Preserve Hideki Kazama art credit without treating the credit alone as route proof.
Separate this row from Unown J, English Spell of the Unown / Wizards Promo copies, EX Unseen Forces Unown R, Neo Discovery/Neo Destiny Unown cards, and name-only Unown listings.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of front/back, language, card text, surface, edges/corners, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.

narrative.human_title: Unown R: the letter without a Wizards shadow
narrative.why_it_matters: Unown R is easy to flatten into alphabet filler, but that is exactly the trap. It belongs to CoroCoro November 2000, not a booster run, and its English absence in the Wizards era makes it different from Unown J even though collectors naturally pair them. The route is the meaning: magazine insert, Japanese unnumbered promo, Kazama letter-creature, and a localization gap that an agent has to keep visible.
